source_text:
Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί, ἀφορμὴν λαβόντες οὐ μικρὰν εἰς τὸ μετανοῆσαι, καιρὸν ἔχοντες ἐπιστρέψωμεν ἐπὶ τὸν καλέσαντα ἡμᾶς θεόν, ἕως ἔτι ἔχομεν τὸν παραδεχόμενον ἡμᾶς.
ἐὰν γὰρ ταῖς ἡδυπαθείαις ταύταις ἀποταξώμεθα καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἡμῶν νικήσωμεν ἐν τῷ μὴ ποιεῖν τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῆς τὰς πονηράς, μεταληψόμεθα τοῦ ἐλέους Ἰησοῦ.
γινώσκετε δέ, ὅτι ἔρχεται ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα τῆς κρίσεως ὡς κλίβανος καιόμενος, καὶ τακήσονταί τινες τῶν οὐρανῶν καὶ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ ὡς μόλιβος ἐπὶ πυρὶ τηκόμενος: καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὰ κρύφια καὶ φανερὰ ἔργα τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
καλὸν οὖν ἐλεημοσύνη ὡς μετάνοια ἁμαρτίας: κρείσσων νηστεία προσευχῆς, ἐλεημοσύνη δὲ ἀμφοτέρων: ἀγάπη δὲ καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν, προσευχὴ δὲ ἐκ καλῆς συνειδήσεως ἐκ θανάτου ῥύεται. μακάριος πᾶς ὁ εὑρεθεὶς ἐν τούτοις πλήρης: ἐλεημοσύνη γὰρ κούφισμα ἁμαρτίας γίνεται.
thought_title: Repent while the day of judgment approaches
orientation: The preacher has just warned that the words of the promise bring condemnation to those who refuse to listen, and now urges the congregation to seize the opportunity for repentance before judgment arrives.
pass_a_gloss: So then, brothers, [having] taken an opportunity not small for [the] repenting, [and] having time, let us turn to the God who called us, while still we have the one who accepts us. For if to these pleasures we renounce and our soul we conquer in the not doing its desires the evil [ones], we will share in the mercy of Jesus. But know that comes already the day of judgment as an oven burning, and will melt some of the heavens and all the earth as lead on fire melting; and then will appear the hidden and open works of men. Good then [is] almsgiving as repentance of sin; better [is] fasting than prayer, but almsgiving than both; but love covers a multitude of sins, but prayer from a good conscience from death rescues. Blessed [is] everyone who is found in these [things] full; for almsgiving a relief of sin becomes.

choices.why: Keeps the litotes 'not small' as in the source, which emphasizes the greatness of the opportunity.
The participle is present and active, describing God's ongoing welcome; 'accepts' preserves the personal, receiving sense.

choices.term: ἐν τῷ μὴ ποιεῖν τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῆς τὰς πονηράς
choices.english: by not carrying out its evil desires
choices.why: The articular infinitive with ἐν expresses means; 'carrying out' renders ποιεῖν with desires as object idiomatically.
rejected: in the not doing of its evil desires
by not doing its evil desires

choices.why: The participle καιόμενος is passive ('being burned' or 'burning'), and 'burning oven' is the natural English idiom for a furnace in operation.
rejected: like a furnace that is lit

choices.why: The genitive προσευχῆς is comparative after κρείσσων; the terse Greek comparison is rendered with 'than' for clarity.
κούφισμα means a lightening or alleviation; 'relief from sin' captures the sense that almsgiving lightens the burden of sin.

bible_refs.note: ἡ ἡμέρα τῆς κρίσεως ὡς κλίβανος καιόμενος echoes 'the day comes burning like an oven' (Malachi 4:1 LXX: ἡμέρα κυρίου ἐρχομένη ὡς κλίβανος καιόμενος).
ἀγάπη δὲ καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν matches 'love covers a multitude of sins' (1 Peter 4:8; cf. Proverbs 10:12).

pass_b_english: So then, brothers and sisters, we have received no small opportunity to repent. Since we still have time, let us turn to the God who called us, while the one who accepts us is still available to us.
For if we renounce these pleasures and master our soul by refusing to carry out its evil desires, we will share in the mercy of Jesus.

You know that the day of judgment is already coming like a burning oven. Some of the heavens will melt, and all the earth will melt like lead in a fire. Then the hidden and visible deeds of human beings will be exposed.

Almsgiving is good, then, as repentance for sin. Fasting is better than prayer, but almsgiving is better than both. Love covers a multitude of sins, and prayer from a good conscience rescues from death. Blessed is everyone who is found full of these things, for almsgiving becomes a relief from sin.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'as repentance of sin' (genitive), English 'for sin' changes sense: almsgiving is good, functioning as repentance from sin, not repentance offered for sin. 'for sin' misrepresents the genitive.
last_rejected.ruling: Genitive ἁμαρτίας with μετάνοια naturally means 'repentance for sin'; English 'for' is a valid rendering of the genitive relationship.

last_rejected.quote: while the one who accepts us is still available to us
last_rejected.source_quote: ἕως ἔτι ἔχομεν τὸν παραδεχόμενον ἡμᾶς
last_rejected.why: English adds 'available to us' not in source; source simply says 'while we still have the one who accepts us'.
last_rejected.fix: while we still have one who accepts us
last_rejected.ruling: ἕως ἔτι ἔχομεν τὸν παραδεχόμενον ἡμᾶς means 'while we still have the one who accepts us'; 'available to us' paraphrases ἔχομεν acceptably.

polish.changed: Clarified the addressee as 'brothers and sisters' to match the congregation, smoothed sentence order and rhythm for reading aloud, and kept every claim and qualification intact.

notes.why: The congregation is addressed with two different forms; reader may wonder if different groups are meant.
notes.fix: Use one form consistently, or note that both mean the same congregation.

notes.quote: Fasting is better than prayer, but almsgiving is better than both
notes.why: This hierarchy of practices is stated without explanation; reader may find it puzzling or arbitrary.
notes.fix: Note: this echoes Tobit 12:8–9, a deuterocanonical text familiar to early Christians.

problems.why: The congregation is addressed with three different forms; a reader may wonder if different groups or tones are intended.
problems.fix: Standardize to one form throughout, or note that all forms address the same congregation.

problems.quote: conquer our soul by refusing to carry out its evil desires
problems.why: 'Conquer our soul' sounds like defeating the self rather than mastering fleshly desires; the Greek likely means 'subdue the flesh' or 'master our desires.'
problems.fix: Render as 'master our desires' or 'subdue our fleshly impulses.'

edits.old: conquer our soul by refusing to carry out its evil desires
edits.new: master our soul by refusing to carry out its evil desires

fixed: Brothers: The source uses ἀδελφοί, which the brief's glossary does not ban, and the English 'brothers and sisters' is a standard inclusive rendering. No change needed.

Conquer our soul: The source ψυχὴν ἡμῶν νικήσωμεν means 'conquer/overcome our soul,' not 'subdue the flesh' (σάρξ is not used here). 'Conquer' is accurate; however, 'master' is a slightly more natural English rendering of νικάω in this context, so I changed it to 'master our soul' to avoid the implication of defeating the self.
